tldr: The headline is an observable criterion for whether an uncensored optimal proximal survival bridge remains efficient after right censoring, together with its exact excess-variance identity. The factual target is \(\psi_{\mathrm{obs}}(P,h)=E_P[H(W,X)]\), identified as the causal survival contrast under every compatible latent law. A probability-weighted conditional projection residual gives a computable diagnostic, with a worked 48-cell implementation. Positive latent realization and actual bridge-preserving score paths justify the causal gradient family with finite negative-control proxies and potentially continuous baseline covariates and event times. A legal open strict-gap region and an attaining finite-support one-step estimator give the criterion an operational use. On the generic smooth finite-proxy IPCW/PDR selector class with saturated censor fitting, the one-step variance is weakly smaller, ties selectors equal to \(v_G\), and strictly improves selectors retaining \(v_F\) wherever \(\mathfrak d_G>0\). Continuous-covariate inference requires explicit nuisance product rates.
gap: Uncensored optimal-bridge efficiency and generic censoring noncommutation do not supply an observable proximal retention criterion on an actual positive one-horizon causal chart. The source survival IPCW/PDR inference theorem does not settle that criterion in the unequal finite-proxy regime.
fill: Theorem 4 gives the sole headline: \(\mathfrak d_G=0\) characterizes retention and \(\mathcal L_G=E_P[\kappa_G(v_F-v_G)^2]\) quantifies loss. Positive causal score lifting justifies its model scope. The diagnostic construction gives an observable small-instance procedure; the rational experiment certifies nonemptiness. Proposition 3 characterizes the exact loss for every smooth finite-proxy IPCW/PDR selector with saturated censor fitting, including equality at \(v_G\) and strict loss for retained \(v_F\). The inference results attain the benchmark on their stated subclasses.
